title: Focus Is On but Apps Still Open? Add an App Block
description: Focus silences notifications but can leave apps available. Add a separate iPhone app block, test access and keep essential communication available.
direct: iPhone Focus can quiet alerts while still letting you open the app. If opening it is the distraction, set a separate block and test that app directly.

cards.decision.heading: Try opening the app
cards.decision.body: Hiding a Home Screen page can reduce visible prompts, but it is a different action from restricting the selected app. Check what happens when you launch it, rather than judging only whether notifications arrive.
sections.detail-0-0.heading: Two tools, two checks
sections.detail-0-0.body: Apple describes Focus as a way to manage interruptions and Screen Time as the place for app-use restrictions. You can use both, but this guide does not claim they automatically activate each other. Notification silence and blocked access each need their own check.
sections.detail-1-0.heading: Use a realistic boundary
sections.detail-1-0.body: One scheduled rule and unlimited thirty-minute Block Now sessions are free; Pro adds scheduled rules. Temporary unlocks offer five, fifteen or thirty minutes.
sections.detail-1-1.heading: Check other ways to open the service
sections.detail-1-1.body: The current listing does not promise a Focus automation, Mac blocking or domain-level website blocking. Another device or browser can remain a separate route to the same service. Choose a small, testable phone routine and keep the permissions and selected apps under review. Optional motivational reminders can remain off if you prefer a quiet setup.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Does switching on Focus start a Dying Soon block automatically?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: This workflow uses separate controls. Start a block or set its schedule in Dying Soon, then check access while it is active.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: What if the app icon is hidden but the app still opens from search?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Hiding an icon changes what you see. Try opening the selected app during an active Screen Time block to check whether access is restricted.

related.related.label: Block Distracting Apps for a 30-Minute Study Session
steps.step-1.text: Keep the Focus settings that manage the calls and alerts you want. Decide separately which distracting apps should be unavailable during the session.
steps.step-2.text: In Dying Soon: Screen Time Limit, authorize Screen Time, select those apps and start a thirty-minute Block Now session or set an available scheduled rule.
steps.step-3.text: While the block is active, try opening a selected app and check that the restriction appears. Confirm that essential communication remains available. Check again when the session ends.
